jurisdiction.handoffTitle: Hand off to your members of Congress
jurisdiction.handoffText: The package goes to the offices of your U.S. representative and both of your state's senators. Each office decides whether to adopt the policy. The public record stays open either way.
jurisdiction.timing: An office can adopt a policy like this at any time. The 120th Congress convenes January 3, 2027.

issue.name: A public channel to your representatives
issue.title: Should your representatives offer a public, verifiable way to work with them?
facts: In September 2025, 17% of Americans said they trust the federal government to do what is right just about always or most of the time.
Google shut down its free Representatives API in 2025. It was a common way for apps to turn an address into a list of officials.
The U.S. Census Bureau's free geocoder returns every congressional, state legislative, county, and school district for a U.S. address.
In Taiwan, the vTaiwan process used the open-source tool Pol.is to find rough consensus among opposing groups. A crowdsourced bill on closely held companies later passed the legislature.

Ireland's Citizens' Assembly brought together 99 randomly selected citizens, broadly representative of the country. Its recommendations on a long-deadlocked constitutional question led to a national referendum in 2018.
lists: What a tool like this would do
Confirm participants are registered voters in the district, without linking who they are to how they vote
Count votes with open code and publish a record anyone can recount
Show where people with different views agree, and where they don't
Send the result to the office, which answers publicly
sources: Pew Research Center: Public trust in government, 1958–2025
Google: notice of turndown of the Representatives API
groups: In these sample votes, agreed more often with keeping it independent of government and privately funded.
In these sample votes, agreed more often with government running or funding it, with public accountability.

statements.text: Residents should have a public way to talk through issues together and send proposals to their representatives.
statements.billText: Offer constituents a public way to talk through issues together and send proposals to this office

statements.text: Every office that receives a proposal should answer it publicly and give its reasons.
statements.billText: Answer every proposal it receives publicly, with its reasons

statements.text: Votes in a tool like this should be counted by open-source code that anyone can check.
statements.billText: Use only tools whose votes are counted by code anyone can read and check

statements.text: AI can help summarize and draft, but it should never count votes or decide anything.
statements.billText: Use AI only to help summarize and draft, never to count votes or decide anything

statements.text: Only registered voters in the district, each confirmed, should take part: one voter, one voice.
statements.billText: Count only verified constituents, one person, one voice

statements.text: Results should show a randomly chosen citizen panel beside the open results.
statements.billText: Show a randomly chosen citizen panel's results beside the open results

statements.text: Government itself should run a tool like this.
A nonpartisan university or nonprofit should run it, not government.
Public money should pay for a pilot in a few states or districts.
Public hearings and comment periods already give residents enough of a voice.

open.label: Verified voters
open.how: Registered voters in the district who chose to join, each confirmed as a real, active voter. Sample data.

panel.label: Citizen panel
panel.how: Chosen by lottery from verified voters, balanced to match the district by age and area, and paid a stipend for their time.
